title: A simple new approach to variable selection in regression, with application to genetic fine mapping.
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B, Statistical methodology
key_point: Sum-of-single-effects regression yields per-variant posterior inclusion probabilities (PIP) and credible sets that each contain a causal variant with stated coverage (e.g. 95%).

title: Fine-mapping from summary data with the "Sum of Single Effects" model.
key_point: Extends SuSiE to GWAS summary statistics plus an LD reference; LD mismatch between sumstats and reference is a key failure mode.

title: FINEMAP: efficient variable selection using summary data from genome-wide association studies.
key_point: Shotgun stochastic search over causal configurations from summary data; alternative to SuSiE producing PIPs.

title: Improving fine-mapping by modeling infinitesimal effects.
key_point: SuSiE/FINEMAP/COJO-ABF can be overconfident (high replication failure rate on downsampling); SuSiE-inf/FINEMAP-inf model infinitesimal background and improve calibration. Open Targets now uses SuSiE-inf.

title: From genome-wide associations to candidate causal variants by statistical fine-mapping.
key_point: Review of LD, statistical fine-mapping, trans-ethnic fine-mapping and annotation integration; lead SNP is not necessarily causal.

title: Functionally informed fine-mapping and polygenic localization of complex trait heritability.
key_point: PolyFun functional priors increase the number of variants with PIP>0.95 by >20% in simulation and >32% across 49 UKB traits vs non-functional SuSiE.

title: Genetic and epigenetic fine mapping of causal autoimmune disease variants.
key_point: Fine-mapping of 21 autoimmune diseases: ~90% of causal variants are non-coding; only 10-20% directly alter recognisable TF motifs.

title: Fine-mapping inflammatory bowel disease loci to single-variant resolution.
key_point: Large-sample IBD fine-mapping resolved a subset of loci to single variants, showing most GWAS loci are not single-variant resolved without very large N.

title: MultiSuSiE improves multi-ancestry fine-mapping in All of Us whole-genome sequencing data.
key_point: MultiSuSiE (All of Us WGS) finds substantially more PIP>0.9 variants than European-only SuSiE; diverse ancestry narrows credible sets.

title: An open approach to systematically prioritize causal variants and genes at all published human GWAS trait-associated loci.
key_point: Open Targets Genetics: systematic fine-mapping + Locus-to-Gene (L2G) ML model trained on 445 gold-standard loci outperforms nearest-gene; L2G genes enriched for approved drug targets (OR 8.1).

title: Open Targets Platform: facilitating therapeutic hypotheses building in drug discovery.
key_point: Open Targets Platform 2025 update integrates GWAS credible sets, L2G and colocalisation into the Platform (Genetics portal merged).

title: Bayesian test for colocalisation between pairs of genetic association studies using summary statistics.
key_point: Bayesian coloc estimates posterior probability H4 that two traits share one causal variant (single-causal-variant assumption).

title: A more accurate method for colocalisation analysis allowing for multiple causal variants.
key_point: Combining coloc with SuSiE relaxes the single-causal-variant assumption and improves accuracy at multi-signal loci.

title: Integration of summary data from GWAS and eQTL studies predicts complex trait gene targets.
key_point: SMR tests whether a trait effect is mediated through expression; HEIDI tests against linkage (distinct causal variants). Many prioritised genes were not the nearest gene.

title: Integrative approaches for large-scale transcriptome-wide association studies.
key_point: TWAS imputes expression from genotype and tests gene-trait association; gene-level signals reflect predicted expression, not proof of causality.

title: Opportunities and challenges for transcriptome-wide association studies.
key_point: TWAS associations are confounded by LD and co-regulation; multiple genes at a locus can be significant and TWAS hits are not causal genes per se.

title: Systematic differences in discovery of genetic effects on gene expression and complex traits.
key_point: GWAS and eQTL studies are systematically biased toward different variant types (eQTLs near TSS, low-constraint genes), limiting colocalisation.

title: The missing link between genetic association and regulatory function.
key_point: Limited evidence that baseline expression explains GWAS signals: colocalisation implicated ~8% of genes; TWAS ~2%.

title: Leveraging polygenic enrichments of gene features to predict genes underlying complex traits and diseases.
key_point: Polygenic priority score uses genome-wide gene features to rank genes at loci; complementary to locus-local evidence.

title: Genome-wide enhancer maps link risk variants to disease genes.
key_point: Activity-by-contact enhancer-gene maps link non-coding risk variants to target genes across cell types.

title: An effector index to predict target genes at GWAS loci.
key_point: Effector index ML model; coding variants, distance and open chromatin are top features for target-gene prediction.

title: Realizing the promise of genome-wide association studies for effector gene prediction.
key_point: Perspective: field has not converged on standards for generating or reporting effector-gene predictions; argues for accessible, evidence-transparent reporting.

title: Predicted Effector Gene Aggregation, Standards and Unified Schema (PEGASUS): A Community Framework for Effector Gene Reporting.
venue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
key_point: PEGASUS (preprint, 2026): metadata standard, per-locus evidence matrix and concise predicted-effector-gene list. Not peer reviewed.

title: Refining the impact of genetic evidence on clinical success.
key_point: Drug programmes with human genetic support are more likely to succeed; benefit rises with confidence in the causal gene.

title: Are drug targets with genetic support twice as likely to be approved? Revised estimates of the impact of genetic support for drug mechanisms on the probability of drug approval.
key_point: Genetic evidence where causal gene is clear (Mendelian or coding GWAS) more than doubles approval probability.

title: Estimation of the multiple testing burden for genomewide association studies of nearly all common variants.
key_point: Estimated ~1 million independent common-variant tests in Europeans (twice in Africans), basis for P<5e-8.

title: Replication validity of genetic association studies.
key_point: Between-study heterogeneity is frequent; first studies correlate only modestly with later ones and tend to overestimate effects.

title: A comprehensive review of genetic association studies.
venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
key_point: Of 166 associations studied >=3 times, only 6 were consistently replicated.

title: Assessment of cumulative evidence on genetic associations: interim guidelines.
key_point: Venice interim guidelines grade cumulative evidence on amount of evidence, replication and protection from bias (A/B/C each) into strong/moderate/weak credibility.

title: A Bayesian measure of the probability of false discovery in genetic epidemiology studies.
key_point: Bayesian false-discovery probability combines prior probability, power and observed data; more interpretable than P-values.

title: Bayes factors for genome-wide association studies: comparison with P-values.
key_point: P-values are hard to calibrate across MAF and sample size; approximate Bayes factors give consistent evidence measure.

title: Assessing the probability that a positive report is false: an approach for molecular epidemiology studies.
venue: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
key_point: False-positive report probability incorporates prior and power to judge noteworthiness of significant findings.

first_author: NCI-NHGRI Working Group on Replication in Association Studies
title: Replicating genotype-phenotype associations.
key_point: NCI-NHGRI working group criteria for replication: same SNP, same direction, same phenotype, adequate power, independent sample.

title: Statistical correction of the Winner's Curse explains replication variability in quantitative trait genome-wide association studies.
key_point: Correcting for winner's curse explains replication rate in same-ancestry samples; ancestry differences cause worse-than-expected replication through LD differences.

title: Accurate modeling of replication rates in genome-wide association studies by accounting for Winner's Curse and study-specific heterogeneity.
key_point: Framework modelling replication with winner's curse and confounding distinguishes noise from confounding as reason for non-replication.

title: No Support for Historical Candidate Gene or Candidate Gene-by-Interaction Hypotheses for Major Depression Across Multiple Large Samples.
key_point: Large-sample test found no support for 18 historical depression candidate genes; candidate-gene literature largely false positives.

title: Most reported genetic associations with general intelligence are probably false positives.
key_point: Most reported candidate-gene associations with intelligence failed to replicate in well-powered samples.

title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity.
key_point: In a large longevity case-control sample, except APOE none of the selected candidate genes replicated.

title: Genome-wide association study (GWAS)-identified disease risk alleles do not compromise human longevity.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
key_point: Nonagenarians carried as many GWAS disease risk alleles as young controls.

title: LongevityMap: a database of human genetic variants associated with longevity.
key_point: LongevityMap database of variants studied in human longevity (source of v1 module), includes negative and positive candidate-gene results.

title: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans.
key_point: Centenarian GWAS behind 280 of v1's study-cited rsIDs; genetic signature design.

title: RETRACTED: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans.
key_point: Earlier Science version of the centenarian genetic-signature study was retracted (genotyping/QC artefact problems) - cautionary example for centenarian vs young-control designs.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies a single major locus contributing to survival into old age; the APOE locus revisited.
key_point: Of 62 prioritised SNPs only the APOE locus reached genome-wide significance for survival to old age (OR 0.71).

title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis of human longevity identifies a novel locus conferring survival beyond 90 years of age.
key_point: 5q33.3 (EBF1 region) associated with survival beyond 90; minor allele associates with lower BP in midlife.

title: GWAS of longevity in CHARGE consortium confirms APOE and FOXO3 candidacy.
venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
key_point: CHARGE GWAS of survival >=90 replicated only APOE and FOXO3 among earlier findings.

title: FOXO3A genotype is strongly associated with human longevity.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
key_point: Original FOXO3A association with longevity in Japanese-American men (candidate-gene design).

title: Association of FOXO3A variation with human longevity confirmed in German centenarians.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
key_point: Replication of FOXO3A in German centenarians, both sexes.

title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies multiple longevity genes.
key_point: Meta-analysis using 90th/99th survival percentile cases vs <=60th percentile controls; APOE e4 lowers and e2 raises odds; GPR78 locus novel.

title: Variants near CHRNA3/5 and APOE have age- and sex-related effects on human lifespan.
key_point: APOE e4 -1.24 years maternal lifespan per allele; CHRNA3/5 -0.86 years paternal; effects strongly age- and sex-dependent.

title: Genome-wide meta-analysis associates HLA-DQA1/DRB1 and LPA and lifestyle factors with human longevity.
key_point: 606,059 parental lifespans: HLA-DQA1/DRB1 and LPA novel; uses 10% hazard = 1 year rule and doubles parent-imputed effects; MR: +1 BMI unit = -7 months.

title: Human longevity: 25 genetic loci associated in 389,166 UK biobank participants.
key_point: 25 loci across parental attained-age phenotypes, many overlapping known disease loci; extreme (top 10%) parental survival analysed separately.

title: Genomics of 1 million parent lifespans implicates novel pathways and common diseases and distinguishes survival chances.
key_point: 1M parental lifespans; replicated FOXO3 and 5q33.3/EBF1 with smaller effects; contradictory evidence at IL6, ANKRD20A9P, USP42, TMTC2; effects reported as years per allele.

title: Multivariate genomic scan implicates novel loci and haem metabolism in human ageing.
key_point: Multivariate healthspan/lifespan/longevity scan identifies further loci and haem metabolism.

title: A Prospective Analysis of Genetic Variants Associated with Human Lifespan.
key_point: 650k-person meta-analysis: 15 parental lifespan loci; common SNPs explain up to 8% of lifespan variance.

title: Rare genetic associations with human lifespan in UK Biobank are enriched for oncogenic genes.
key_point: UKB survival exome study: LoF burden in TET2, ATM, BRCA2, BRCA1, ASXL1 etc. linked to reduced lifespan; signals largely cancer/CHIP-driven.

title: Genome-wide association study reveals BET1L associated with survival time in the 137,693 Japanese individuals.
key_point: Japanese (137,693) survival-time GWAS identifies BET1L; illustrates ancestry-specific discovery.

title: Age-stratified genomic analyses reveal population-specific genetic determinants of exceptional longevity in Taiwan.
key_point: Taiwanese age-stratified longevity GWAS: population-specific determinants, age-dependent architecture.

title: Sex Differences in Genetic Associations With Longevity.
key_point: Chinese centenarian sex-stratified GWAS/PRS shows sex differences in longevity associations.

title: APOE Alleles and Extreme Human Longevity.
venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
key_point: APOE e4 lowers odds of extreme longevity and raises death risk even beyond ages reached by <1%; e2 protective but with modest effect at the most extreme ages.

title: Varying Effects of APOE Alleles on Extreme Longevity in European Ethnicities.
venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
key_point: APOE effects on extreme longevity vary across European sub-ancestries (weaker e2/e4 effects in a Southern-Italian-enriched cluster).

title: Evidence of survival bias in the association between APOE-Є4 and age at ischemic stroke onset.
key_point: APOE e4 association with later stroke onset likely reflects survival bias rather than stroke biology.

title: Modeling APOE, morbidity, and mortality: a reproducibility challenge for genetic epidemiology.
key_point: APOE-mortality findings are sensitive to analytic choices: rare-genotype exclusion, baseline model, adjustment for non-confounders; age-dependent effects and selective survival.

title: Adjustment for index event bias in genome-wide association studies of subsequent events.
key_point: Selecting on disease status biases genetic associations with prognosis/survival; proposes residual-based adjustment.

title: Collider scope: when selection bias can substantially influence observed associations.
key_point: Selection into a study on factors related to exposure and outcome can create or distort associations.

title: Survival Bias in Mendelian Randomization Studies: A Threat to Causal Inference.
key_point: Survival bias can distort MR estimates, especially when exposure affects survival and the outcome is at older age.

title: Comparison of Sociodemographic and Health-Related Characteristics of UK Biobank Participants With Those of the General Population.
key_point: UK Biobank participants healthier and less deprived than the general population (healthy volunteer bias).

title: Participation bias in the UK Biobank distorts genetic associations and downstream analyses.
key_point: Weighting UKB for representativeness changes SNP effect sizes and genetic correlations; participation bias distorts genetic associations.

title: Case-control association mapping by proxy using family history of disease.
key_point: Using relatives' disease status as proxy phenotype (GWAX) - related to parental-lifespan kin-cohort designs, where the proxy dilutes the per-allele effect (parent shares half the genome).

title: Estimates of the Heritability of Human Longevity Are Substantially Inflated due to Assortative Mating.
key_point: True heritability of lifespan likely <10%; assortative mating inflated earlier estimates - sets low ceiling for SNP-level prediction.

title: Quantitative analysis of population-scale family trees with millions of relatives.
key_point: Population-scale family trees used to partition genetic architecture of longevity; birth-cohort context.

title: Principal components analysis corrects for stratification in genome-wide association studies.
key_point: PCA (EIGENSTRAT) corrects for population stratification in GWAS.

title: Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities.
key_point: Polygenic risk prediction transfers poorly to non-European ancestries; diversity needed.

title: A standardized, evidence-based protocol to assess clinical actionability of genetic disorders associated with genomic variation.
venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
key_point: ClinGen semi-quantitative actionability protocol: severity, likelihood, efficacy, nature of intervention, knowledge base.

title: Implementing evidence-based assertions of clinical actionability in the context of secondary findings: Updates from the ClinGen Actionability Working Group.
venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
key_point: ClinGen AWG added assertions on a 4-point scale (limited/moderate/strong/definitive) for gene-condition pairs.

title: A Standardized Framework to Assess the Clinical Actionability of Genes and Associated Conditions for Population-Based Genomic Screening.
key_point: ClinGen framework adapted for population genomic screening in adults (penetrance certainty, cost-effectiveness).

title: ACMG SF v3.3 list for reporting of secondary findings in clinical exome and genome sequencing: A policy statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG).
venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
key_point: ACMG SF v3.3 policy statement updating the secondary-findings gene list.

title: Prioritizing genomic applications for action by level of evidence: a horizon-scanning method.
key_point: CDC horizon-scanning method assigns genomic applications to evidence tiers (basis of Tier 1: HBOC, Lynch, FH).

title: Genetic identification of familial hypercholesterolemia within a single U.S. health care system.
key_point: Genomic screening identified FH carriers, most under-treated; only 24% met clinical FH criteria.

title: Population genetic screening efficiently identifies carriers of autosomal dominant diseases.
key_point: Population screening for tier-1 conditions found carriers mostly undetected in routine care; only 25% reported relevant family history.

title: Protective lipid-lowering variants in healthy older individuals without coronary heart disease.
key_point: Rare PCSK9/APOB variants and PCSK9 R46L (rs11591147-T) lower LDL-C in healthy >=70-year-olds.

title: Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
key_point: PCSK9 loss-of-function variants lower LDL-C and protect against coronary heart disease.

first_author: Interleukin-6 Receptor Mendelian Randomisation Analysis (IL6R MR) Consortium
title: The interleukin-6 receptor as a target for prevention of coronary heart disease: a mendelian randomisation analysis.
key_point: IL6R Asp358Ala MR supports IL-6 receptor as a CHD target.

title: Genetic and Pharmacologic Inactivation of ANGPTL3 and Cardiovascular Disease.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
key_point: ANGPTL3 loss-of-function lowers lipids and ASCVD odds; therapeutic antagonism mirrors genetics.

first_author: TG and HDL Working Group of the Exome Sequencing Project, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
title: Loss-of-function mutations in APOC3, triglycerides, and coronary disease.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
key_point: APOC3 loss-of-function lowers triglycerides and CHD risk (OR 0.60).

title: HMG-coenzyme A reductase inhibition, type 2 diabetes, and bodyweight: evidence from genetic analysis and randomised trials.
key_point: HMGCR variants mimic statin effects including small T2D and weight increase.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and aortic stenosis: a European Atherosclerosis Society consensus statement.
key_point: EAS consensus: Lp(a) causal for ASCVD and aortic stenosis; supports measuring Lp(a) at least once in adults.

title: Genetic Risk, Adherence to a Healthy Lifestyle, and Coronary Disease.
venue: The New England journal of medicine
key_point: Favourable lifestyle associated with lower CAD risk across genetic risk strata - genetic risk is not destiny.
